items.finding: When testing strong-form betting-market efficiency, normalized/no-vig probabilities are the appropriate probability input; regressions using raw inverse odds can be biased toward falsely accepting efficiency.
items.guidance: Keep no-vig normalization as the default live benchmark and historical-calibration basis.

provenance.legacyCitation: Whelan & Hegarty / Sports Economics Review 2024, Comparing two methods for testing the efficiency of sports betting markets

items.finding: Major sports betting markets are generally highly informative and often efficient within transaction costs; statistical biases do not automatically imply profitable bets after vig.
items.guidance: Treat market price as a strong prior, not an opponent to be ignored. Require multiple independent signals before overriding it.

provenance.legacyCitation: Efficiency of Racing, Sports, and Lottery Betting Markets, Handbook of Sports and Lottery Markets (2008)

items.finding: Favorite-longshot bias is widespread, but its sign and magnitude vary by sport, market structure, and bookmaker. Longshots often have worse expected returns, but MLB/NHL and some U.S. side markets have historically shown reverse patterns.
items.guidance: Never apply a universal favorite/longshot correction. Use sport/market-specific calibration.

provenance.legacyCitation: Ottaviani & Sørensen 2008; Whelan 2024/2026 market-structure work

items.finding: Individual bookmakers can fail to incorporate information already present in competitors' odds; aggregated/market-best information can be more informative than a single book.
items.guidance: Preserve line shopping and consensus/sharp benchmarking. Do not treat one book as the truth.

provenance.legacyCitation: Elaad, Reade & Singleton 2020, Information, prices and efficiency in an online betting market

items.finding: Line movement often improves forecast accuracy from opener to close because informed trading/news is incorporated, although specific markets and early-season regimes can retain biases.
items.guidance: Use close/near-close as the strongest market benchmark and track whether Betting Edge recommendations beat it (CLV).

provenance.legacyCitation: Gandar et al. 1998 NBA; NBA player-absence study 2015; later line-movement research

items.finding: MLB moneyline research repeatedly documented a reverse favorite-longshot bias, but deviations were generally insufficient to yield simple profitable strategies after commissions.
items.guidance: Use as a prior/guardrail, not a mechanical dog/favorite system. Revalidate in current multi-book MLB data.

provenance.legacyCitation: Woodland & Woodland 1994; 2003 update

items.finding: Research examining MLB sportsbook behavior found no statistically significant returns from simply betting against the public.
items.guidance: Do not use public splits alone as a BET reason; retain only as secondary context.

provenance.legacyCitation: Paul & Weinbach, Behavioral Biases and Sportsbook Pricing in Major League Baseball, Oxford Handbook 2012

items.finding: Detailed MLB line-movement research finds forecasts mostly reliable but some repeatable intraday movement inefficiencies; newer work extends evidence of negative autocorrelation in moneyline changes across MLB/NFL/NBA/NHL.
items.guidance: Keep movement path, not just opener/closer, where timestamped data exist; test reversal/overreaction patterns in shadow mode.

provenance.legacyCitation: Simon 2024 Management Science; Simon 2025/26 multi-sport movement paper

items.finding: NBA opening-to-closing spread moves historically improve forecast accuracy and tend to remove opening-line biases, consistent with informed trader influence.
items.guidance: Treat meaningful late moves as information; price recommendations against the latest verified line rather than stale openers.

provenance.legacyCitation: Gandar, Dare, Brown & Zuber 1998

items.finding: Opening lines can be biased when important players are absent, but the market tends to correct those biases by game time.
items.guidance: Lineup/injury edge is most valuable before full market incorporation; after a large corrective move, avoid double-counting the news.

provenance.legacyCitation: Player absence and betting lines in the NBA, Finance Research Letters 2015

items.finding: Older research found under-value at very high NBA totals, but a 2012-13 to 2018-19 revisit found the market had become more efficient and earlier thresholds did not transport cleanly.
items.guidance: Treat historical total-threshold systems as era-dependent; re-estimate against current scoring environment.

provenance.legacyCitation: Paul et al. 2004; 2021 revisit

items.finding: Research found early-season NBA totals lines could retain bias even after movement while sides did not show the same effect.
items.guidance: Early-season totals may merit higher uncertainty and targeted current-era validation, not automatic bets.

provenance.legacyCitation: Baryla et al. 2007, Learning, price formation and the early season bias in the NBA

items.finding: Decades of NFL spread research generally finds a highly efficient market, with many historical home/favorite/underdog anomalies shrinking or depending on transaction costs.
items.guidance: Require strong matchup/news/price evidence; avoid generic home-dog/favorite systems without current validation.

provenance.legacyCitation: Gandar et al. 1988; Gray & Gray 1997; generalized home/favorite model 1996

items.finding: A 2003-2016 study found division-rival games were less likely to see the home team cover and less likely to go over, with out-of-sample model results near 57% in selected strategies.
items.guidance: Use divisional familiarity as a secondary feature and revalidate on recent seasons; do not hard-code 57%.

provenance.legacyCitation: Shank 2019, NFL betting market efficiency, divisional rivals, and profitable strategies

items.finding: Historical NFL research found extreme-temperature acclimatization effects were not fully priced in a 1981-2004 sample.
items.guidance: Weather must remain matchup-specific and current; use as a model input, not a fixed historical adjustment.

provenance.legacyCitation: Borghesi 2007, The home team weather advantage and biases in the NFL betting market

items.finding: Recent work on NFL information asymmetry finds that the relationship between betting percentages and moves can carry information, but direction matters and simple majority-fade rules are not generally supported.
items.guidance: Splits should be interpreted together with verified line movement, never alone.

provenance.legacyCitation: Information asymmetry in the NFL gambling market, 2022/23

items.finding: NHL moneyline research has historically documented reverse favorite-longshot behavior, similar to MLB in older literature.
items.guidance: Use as historical prior only; current NHL price bands/movement still need contemporary validation.

provenance.legacyCitation: Referenced in Berkowitz et al. 2017 and prior NHL market-efficiency work by Gandar et al.

items.finding: Compared with NFL/NBA/MLB/soccer, recent peer-reviewed NHL-specific betting research is thinner; historical reverse-FLB findings should not be assumed to hold unchanged in modern multi-book markets.
items.guidance: Our current NHL open-close and movement calibration remains genuinely useful rather than redundant.

provenance.legacyCitation: Research-library synthesis

items.finding: Professional tennis exhibits favorite-longshot bias; one ~45,000-match study found it stronger among lower-ranked players, later rounds, and high-profile tournaments.
items.guidance: Apply sport-specific no-vig calibration by odds band, tour/level/round; avoid treating longshots as equally priced across contexts.

provenance.legacyCitation: Lahvicka 2013, What Causes the Favorite-Longshot Bias? Further Evidence from Tennis

items.finding: Recent fixed-odds research uses tennis as a two-outcome market where favorite-longshot patterns fit models of bookmaker market structure and demand elasticity.
items.guidance: Book-specific margin shape matters; no-vig should be price-sensitive rather than assuming equal margin allocation.

provenance.legacyCitation: Whelan 2026, Market structure and prices in online betting markets

items.finding: A 2026 peer-reviewed MMA study found no general favorite-longshot bias and concluded the market is largely efficient; youth/travel effects and women's-favorite results appeared promising, but out-of-sample positive returns were limited.
items.guidance: Do not import favorite-longshot assumptions from other sports. Treat age/travel/sex effects as research candidates requiring local validation.

provenance.legacyCitation: Miller & Nichols 2026, Efficient market insights and favorite-longshot bias in mixed martial arts betting markets

items.finding: A targeted search did not surface a comparable modern peer-reviewed body of boxing betting-market efficiency work. Fight prediction literature exists, but robust market-pricing research appears much thinner.
items.guidance: Boxing still requires local historical odds calibration; do not borrow MMA conclusions automatically.

provenance.legacyCitation: Research-library search result

items.finding: A targeted search did not surface a substantial peer-reviewed CFL betting-market efficiency literature comparable to NFL/NBA/MLB. CFL remains a genuine local-calibration need.
items.guidance: Continue CFL historical acquisition/calibration; NFL findings are context only, not transferable priors.

provenance.legacyCitation: Research-library search result

items.finding: Large European soccer samples document favorite-longshot bias in bookmaker and exchange markets; market efficiency varies by league and whether mean or best available odds are used.
items.guidance: Line shopping is especially important; analyze league-specific 1X2 calibration and best-price thresholds rather than generic soccer priors.

provenance.legacyCitation: Efficiency of online football betting markets (2019); lottery-type assets study

items.finding: Betting exchanges have been found more accurate than bookmakers in major European soccer samples, and individual bookmakers may not fully incorporate competitor information.
items.guidance: When available, exchange/market-consensus prices are strong fair-value benchmarks.

provenance.legacyCitation: Franck, Verbeek & Nüesch 2010

items.finding: Published modeling work finds the Asian handicap market shares some inefficiencies with traditional 1X2 markets, with important differences by price source and decision threshold.
items.guidance: Build separate Asian-handicap calibration; do not map 1X2 bias mechanically into AH prices.

provenance.legacyCitation: Constantinou 2020, Asian handicap football betting market

items.finding: High-frequency/in-play markets can incorporate major news quickly, but behavioral mispricing around surprise events and near expiry can occur. Efficiency is not constant through time-to-event.
items.guidance: Live bets require a separate model/error margin from pregame; never infer live fair value solely from pregame calibration.

provenance.legacyCitation: Oxford Handbook high-frequency betting markets; 2021 in-play prediction-market study

items.finding: For betting decisions, probability calibration is more relevant than raw classification accuracy because EV depends on the quality of probability estimates at quoted prices.
items.guidance: Evaluate models/signals with calibration, Brier/log loss, CLV and realized EV—not win percentage alone.

provenance.legacyCitation: Walsh & Joshi 2023, Machine learning for sports betting: should model selection be based on accuracy or calibration?

items.finding: A 2004 reexamination corrected commission treatment in earlier NHL work and still found the inefficiency/reverse favorite-longshot result survived the stricter tests.
items.guidance: Confirms old NHL anomaly was not merely a commission-calculation artifact; still requires modern-era validation.

provenance.legacyCitation: Gandar, Zuber & Johnson 2004, Journal of Sports Economics

items.finding: A 2011 extension using ten additional NHL seasons continued to study reverse favorite-longshot behavior and reported profitable wagering opportunities in the historical NHL market.
items.guidance: Raises the priority of modern NHL revalidation, especially by price band and book, but does not justify importing old profit thresholds.

provenance.legacyCitation: Woodland & Woodland 2011, Journal of Sports Economics

items.finding: NFL research using more recent samples found statistical inefficiencies in substantial home underdogs and nonlinear total-line effects, but these are sample-dependent and may not survive modern pricing.
items.guidance: Use as a candidate-feature prior only; current-era holdout testing is mandatory.

provenance.legacyCitation: Shank 2018, Journal of Economics and Finance / SSRN

items.finding: Research has found home-field pricing biases in nationally prominent NFL games and tested similar effects in NBA and MLB; home advantage is not a stable universal betting edge across sports.
items.guidance: Model home advantage sport- and context-specifically; never use a universal home-team premium.

provenance.legacyCitation: Gandar, Zuber & Lamb 2001, Journal of Economics and Business

items.finding: Conventional bookmaker-margin calculations can understate average bettor loss when margins vary by outcome probability; soccer and tennis evidence shows longshots can carry systematically higher effective margins.
items.guidance: Do not assume equal-vig allocation when converting odds to fair probability. Compare multiple de-vig methods and calibrate by sport/book/price.

provenance.legacyCitation: Whelan & Hegarty 2023, Calculating the Bookmaker's Margin

items.finding: Discrete bookmaker odds grids can mechanically create favorite-longshot bias even without behavioral mispricing.
items.guidance: Treat some apparent bias as market-structure/margin shape rather than true predictive error.

provenance.legacyCitation: Koch & Shing 2007

items.finding: In-play prediction-market research finds mispricing can increase following surprising major events, particularly late shocks involving longshots.
items.guidance: Live-event shocks deserve separate recalibration and uncertainty; do not extrapolate pregame fair probabilities mechanically after major state changes.

provenance.legacyCitation: Angelini, De Angelis & Singleton 2022, International Journal of Forecasting

items.finding: A 2026 sports prediction-market study using 23 million trades reports that calibration changes materially near expiry and that parlays become increasingly overpriced with leg count.
items.guidance: Treat near-expiry/live exchange probabilities and parlays as distinct products; do not assume static calibration through time.

provenance.legacyCitation: Moshrefi 2026, arXiv preprint

items.finding: A 2026 study on ~90,000 football matches reports that bookmaker-aware odds-only probability transformations can outperform standard multiplicative, Shin, and Power conversions for many books.
items.guidance: Benchmark our current no-vig method against multiple de-vig transforms rather than assuming multiplicative normalization is always best.

provenance.legacyCitation: Goto, Takeishi & Yairi 2026, arXiv preprint

items.finding: Using four sportsbooks and 3,681 MLB games, a 2024 Management Science paper found forecasts were mostly reliable but some simple strategies based on real-time line movement produced significant historical profits.
items.guidance: Justifies preserving timestamped intra-day movement and testing movement path, not merely opener/closer.

provenance.legacyCitation: Jay Simon 2024, Management Science

items.finding: A study of more than 16,000 English football matches and 51 bookmakers found odds generally unbiased against outcomes while individual books could fail to incorporate information already present in competitors' odds.
items.guidance: Consensus/best-price information can be superior to an individual book's price even when the market overall is efficient.

provenance.legacyCitation: Elaad, Reade & Singleton 2020, Finance Research Letters

items.finding: A 33,060-match, 41-bookmaker study across 11 European leagues found efficiency and favorite-longshot behavior vary across national competitions.
items.guidance: Soccer calibration must remain league-specific; never pool all leagues into one 1X2 prior.

provenance.legacyCitation: Angelini & De Angelis 2019, International Journal of Forecasting

items.finding: A 2026 review synthesizes behavioral, informational and structural explanations for favorite-longshot bias and proposes bookmaker hedging as an additional mechanism.
items.guidance: Use FLB as a calibration phenomenon, not evidence of a single bettor-psychology mechanism.

provenance.legacyCitation: Bakalo 2026, SSRN

items.finding: A 2022 Journal of Business Analytics paper used CFL play-by-play and wagering data from 2015-2019 to build logistic-regression and gradient-boosting in-game win-probability models. Models using pregame spread and total information were well calibrated.
items.guidance: CFL live markets need their own calibrated state model. Pregame spread/total should be treated as strong priors in live CFL analysis, not ignored.

provenance.legacyCitation: Hill 2022, In-game win probability models for Canadian football

items.finding: Since 2023 the CFL and Genius Sports have operated CFL LiveStats as the league's official play-by-play and post-game data system, including support for live betting data distribution.
items.guidance: Prefer official CFL event/play-by-play identity for current/live analysis and use historical third-party odds only for market calibration.

provenance.legacyCitation: CFL / Genius Sports official announcement 2023

items.finding: A 2019-2020 UFC calibration study found fight-winner moneyline odds were calibrated, while method-of-victory and winning-round odds were not.
items.guidance: Separate UFC winner markets from method/round props. Do not inherit moneyline calibration confidence into derivative fight props.

provenance.legacyCitation: Stanhope 2021, Are Money Line Odds in UFC Matches Calibrated?

items.finding: A 2023 International Journal of Forecasting paper modeled MMA contests as Markov processes using fighter skills, compared forecasts with historical bookmaker odds, and reported a betting strategy based on the model.
items.guidance: MMA fair-value work should model how fights can unfold, not only binary fighter ratings; bookmaker prices remain a benchmark against the structural model.

provenance.legacyCitation: Holmes, McHale & Zychaluk 2023

items.finding: A correction/replication of a published tennis mispricing study found that a single erroneous long-odds observation drove much of the reported profitability. After correction, most profits disappeared and later-period replication failed.
items.guidance: Tennis historical edges require outlier checks, odds-integrity gates and post-publication holdouts. One spectacular price must never drive a signal.

provenance.legacyCitation: Clegg & Cartlidge 2023 correction study

items.finding: Using more than 160,000 soccer matches from 2000-01 through 2020-21, research found persistent favorite-longshot and hot-hand biases and argued bookmakers may rationally accommodate bettor biases in their own price setting.
items.guidance: Do not assume bookmaker odds are neutral probability forecasts plus symmetric vig. Book-specific bias and margin shape should be modeled.

provenance.legacyCitation: Goto & Yamada 2023, International Review of Economics & Finance

items.finding: Management Science research using NFL games and lines found no strong inefficiency but showed team abilities vary meaningfully week to week and market participants have more difficulty learning from noisy observations.
items.guidance: Recent performance should be shrinkage-weighted rather than blindly extrapolated; noisy games should receive less influence in team-strength updates.

provenance.legacyCitation: Dana & Knetter 1994, Learning and Efficiency in a Gambling Market

items.finding: A 2021 revisit of older NBA high-total inefficiency found the more recent 2012-13 to 2018-19 market was more efficient and earlier profitable thresholds did not transport cleanly.
items.guidance: Historical thresholds must be era-specific and re-estimated; never freeze old totals cutoffs into the live model.

provenance.legacyCitation: Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance 2021

items.finding: Research found early-season NBA totals lines were biased even after open-to-close movement, while sides did not show the same effect.
items.guidance: Early-season totals deserve a separate uncertainty/calibration regime, but the historical profitable threshold needs current-era revalidation.

provenance.legacyCitation: Finance Research Letters 2007

items.finding: NBA betting experiments found model selection based on probability calibration produced much better betting results than selection based on classification accuracy.
items.guidance: Optimize and evaluate Betting Edge probabilities using calibration, Brier/log loss, CLV and EV—not pick percentage.

provenance.legacyCitation: Walsh & Joshi 2023

items.finding: College football and basketball fixed-odds moneyline markets showed favorite-longshot bias, but heavy-favorite strategies were approximately break-even rather than clearly profitable after transaction costs.
items.guidance: If college sports are added later, use their own price calibration rather than importing professional-league priors.

provenance.legacyCitation: Berkowitz, Depken & Gandar 2017

items.finding: Cross-sport work on NFL, NBA and MLB shows home-field betting effects are context dependent rather than universal.
items.guidance: Home advantage belongs inside sport-specific matchup/fair-value models and should not become a generic historical boost.

provenance.legacyCitation: Gandar, Zuber & Lamb 2001

items.finding: A 2018 doctoral study using NHL closing totals and associated odds found the totals market largely efficient; only one tested heuristic strategy produced a marginal above-average return.
items.guidance: Treat NHL totals as a high-efficiency market by default. Historical total-angle systems need strong current evidence and price verification.

provenance.legacyCitation: Traugutt 2018, The National Hockey League Totals Market: Efficiency, Profitability, and Heuristic Behaviors

items.finding: NHL efficiency can vary with the information environment and time of season; treating the entire season as homogeneous can hide information effects.
items.guidance: Keep season phase and information regime as calibration variables. Do not pool early-season and mature-season NHL blindly.

provenance.legacyCitation: Ryan, Gramm & McKinney 2013, Information Effects and National Hockey League Betting Market Efficiency

items.finding: A 2022 honors thesis using NHL lines/results from 2015-2020 reported an 8.5% ROI when its multivariate probit model was tested on 2020-21.
items.guidance: Useful only as a candidate modeling reference. Do not treat the reported ROI as established until reproduced independently with clean prices and holdout controls.

provenance.legacyCitation: Luxton, Spizman & Moore 2022, Testing Efficiency in NHL Betting Markets

items.finding: NFL out-of-sample betting strategies based on apparent inefficiencies produced mixed persistence, and documented inefficiencies tended to dissipate over time.
items.guidance: Every NFL anomaly gets a recency/holdout test. Published historical profitability is never assumed to survive.

provenance.legacyCitation: Gray & Gray 1997, Testing Market Efficiency: Evidence From The NFL Sports Betting Market

items.finding: A 1994-2000 NFL study found no conclusive evidence of general inefficiency after testing weak-form efficiency, power scores, stadium characteristics and alternative strategies.
items.guidance: Objective matchup features must clear current-price thresholds; descriptive football knowledge alone is unlikely to produce durable edge.

provenance.legacyCitation: Boulier, Stekler & Amundson 2006, Testing the efficiency of the National Football League betting market

items.finding: A consolidated 2004 NFL study found only fairly weak evidence for a home-underdog bias and no significant returns from momentum strategies.
items.guidance: Do not encode generic home-dog or momentum bonuses. Require current price and independent matchup support.

provenance.legacyCitation: Dare & Holland 2004, Efficiency in the NFL betting market: modifying and consolidating research methods

items.finding: A practitioner analysis of 12,624 NFL player-prop bets across DraftKings, ESPN BET, BetMGM and Pinnacle found Pinnacle the sharpest of the four and found probability-conversion methods that account for favorite-longshot-shaped vig improved accuracy.
items.guidance: Player props should use book-aware vig removal and sharp-book comparison when available. This is a design prior, not a production adjustment.

provenance.legacyCitation: Chanchani 2024, Measuring Sportsbook Accuracy: Analysis of NFL Player Props Using Line Deviations

items.finding: Targeted searches still surface far less peer-reviewed calibration/efficiency literature for NBA/NFL/NHL/MLB player props than for game-level sides, moneylines and totals.
items.guidance: Props require local calibration, greater uncertainty margins, lineup/minutes/role modeling, and stricter price verification. Do not inherit confidence from game markets.

provenance.legacyCitation: Betting Edge targeted literature review

items.finding: Recent sportsbook and league integrity cases demonstrate that low-volume individual player props can be unusually sensitive to private information and anomalous action.
items.guidance: For obscure/low-liquidity props, increase uncertainty and require stronger multi-book confirmation. Treat abnormal market movement as information but also as an integrity-risk flag.

provenance.legacyCitation: Current regulated-market integrity reporting

items.finding: A second targeted literature search still did not identify a modern peer-reviewed boxing betting-market efficiency/calibration literature comparable with NFL, NHL, MLB, soccer, tennis or MMA.
items.guidance: Boxing needs its own odds-history calibration. Fight-prediction models and pundit picks cannot substitute for market calibration.

provenance.legacyCitation: Betting Edge targeted literature review

items.finding: Because boxing winner, method-of-victory, round-group and total-round markets have different outcome structures and margins, they should be calibrated independently rather than pooled.
items.guidance: Build fight winner first; only add method/round/total markets when adequate historical prices and sample sizes exist.

provenance.legacyCitation: Betting Edge market-structure inference from available boxing market formats

items.finding: CFL has legitimate in-game win-probability research, but targeted searches still reveal much thinner published pregame spread/moneyline/total efficiency literature than the NFL.
items.guidance: Use CFL published live-model work as methodology, but build pregame calibration locally from historical CFL odds/results.

provenance.legacyCitation: Betting Edge targeted literature review

items.finding: Existing CFL in-game research supports using pregame spread/total information as strong prior features inside calibrated live win-probability models.
items.guidance: When Betting Edge eventually models CFL live markets, anchor state estimates to pregame market priors and update with score/time/possession rather than restarting from scratch.

provenance.legacyCitation: Hill 2022, In-game win probability models for Canadian football

items.finding: Research on COVID-era betting found unusual NBA moneyline inefficiency concentrated in specific underdog ranges, illustrating that structural breaks can temporarily invalidate normal calibration.
items.guidance: Tag unusual eras/rule environments explicitly. Never pool structural-break periods into normal calibration without testing.

provenance.legacyCitation: Qureshi & Zaman 2021, The Impact of COVID-19 on Sports Betting Markets

items.finding: Recent prediction-market research finds apparent in-play arbitrage/mispricing can be real but fleeting and constrained by order-book depth and execution size.
items.guidance: A theoretical live edge is not sufficient; Betting Edge should distinguish quoted edge from executable edge and consider liquidity/timing where relevant.

provenance.legacyCitation: Cheng, Yang & Zou 2026, Arbitrage Analysis in Polymarket NBA Markets

items.finding: Levitt showed that sportsbooks need not simply balance equal money on both sides; bookmakers can exploit bettor biases and set prices strategically while managing exposure.
items.guidance: Do not assume sportsbook prices are neutral forecasts plus symmetric vig. Book identity, clientele and shading can matter.

provenance.legacyCitation: Steven D. Levitt (2004), Why Are Gambling Markets Organised So Differently from Financial Markets?, The Economic Journal

items.finding: Shin developed a bookmaker-pricing model in which possible insider trading changes optimal odds and helps explain asymmetric margin allocation across outcomes.
items.guidance: Supports comparing multiplicative no-vig with Shin-style de-vig rather than assuming equal proportional margin removal is always correct.

provenance.legacyCitation: Hyun Song Shin (1991), Optimal Betting Odds Against Insider Traders, The Economic Journal

items.finding: English football research compared bookmaker prices with statistical forecasting and found odds-setters contain substantial predictive information.
items.guidance: Sportsbook consensus should remain a powerful prior even when Betting Edge has a statistical model; the model must add information rather than replace the market.

provenance.legacyCitation: Forrest, Goddard & Simmons (2005), Odds-setters as forecasters: The case of English football, International Journal of Forecasting

items.finding: Research tested whether statistical football forecasts add value in the UK betting market and highlighted the difference between predictive accuracy and profitable wagering at quoted prices.
items.guidance: Evaluate model signals against sportsbook price/EV, not only whether the predicted team wins.

provenance.legacyCitation: Dixon & Pope (2004), The value of statistical forecasts in the UK association football betting market, International Journal of Forecasting

items.finding: Forecasting research comparing prediction markets, betting odds and tipsters found market-based forecasts highly competitive with expert forecasts.
items.guidance: Named handicappers and pundits should remain secondary contextual signals; market prices and independently measured information stay primary.

provenance.legacyCitation: Spann & Skiera (2009), Sports forecasting: a comparison of the forecast accuracy of prediction markets, betting odds and tipsters, Journal of Forecasting

items.finding: Classic NFL work reported evidence suggesting exploitable structure in point spreads, helping launch the subsequent efficiency debate and many replication studies.
items.guidance: Historical NFL anomalies are useful hypothesis generators, but later research and edge decay mean they require modern holdouts.

provenance.legacyCitation: Zuber, Gandar & Bowers (1985), Beating the Spread: Testing the Efficiency of the Gambling Market for National Football League Games, Journal of Political Economy

items.finding: A subsequent NFL study reexamined earlier claims of spread inefficiency and contributed to the broader conclusion that simple exploitable rules are fragile across samples and methods.
items.guidance: Any NFL historical pattern needs independent replication and true holdout testing before receiving even shadow weight.

provenance.legacyCitation: Sauer, Brajer, Ferris & Marr (1988), Hold Your Bets: Another Look at the Efficiency of the Gambling Market for National Football League Games, Journal of Political Economy

items.finding: An update to the MLB reverse favorite-longshot literature revisited the anomaly with additional data, reinforcing the need to distinguish statistical bias from after-vig profitability.
items.guidance: Keep MLB price-band calibration, but never translate reverse-FLB evidence into a mechanical favorite/dog rule.

provenance.legacyCitation: Woodland & Woodland (2003), The Reverse Favourite-Longshot Bias and Market Efficiency in Major League Baseball: An Update, Bulletin of Economic Research

items.finding: Elo-based football forecasts were evaluated for match-result prediction, providing a durable benchmark for team-strength modeling against market odds.
items.guidance: For soccer, team-strength models such as Elo should be treated as one component of fair value and benchmarked against current market probabilities.

provenance.legacyCitation: Hvattum & Arntzen (2010), Using ELO ratings for match result prediction in association football, International Journal of Forecasting

items.finding: Classic tennis forecasting research modeled match-winning probabilities from player and match information, establishing a quantitative foundation for tennis probability models beyond rankings alone.
items.guidance: ATP/WTA fair-value models should incorporate player-strength and match-context features rather than rely on rank difference alone.

provenance.legacyCitation: Klaassen & Magnus, Forecasting the winner of a tennis match, European Journal of Operational Research

items.legacyLabel: Modern NHL: is there useful recent market-movement evidence?
items.topic: Modern NHL: is there useful recent market-movement evidence?
items.finding: Yes. A 2025 peer-reviewed paper studies NFL, NBA and NHL moneyline movement at three sportsbooks from 2019-2023 and finds significant negative autocorrelation in price changes in each sport, consistent with short-run overreaction.
items.guidance: Preserve intraday movement path for NHL/NFL/NBA. Test reversal/overreaction in shadow mode; do not equate every move with information.

provenance.legacyCitation: Jay Simon (2025), Autocorrelation and Weekend Effects: Inefficiencies in Moneyline Movement for Three Major Sports

items.legacyLabel: Modern NHL totals: is the literature stronger than we thought?
items.topic: Modern NHL totals: is the literature stronger than we thought?
items.finding: Yes. A 2022 Journal of Economic Insight study uses nine seasons of NHL totals data and finds some forecastability, but profitable opportunities are limited. This reinforces an efficient-market prior rather than an easy totals system.
items.guidance: Keep NHL totals as a separate calibrated market; use probabilistic models and price thresholds, not heuristic over/under rules.

provenance.legacyCitation: Alex Traugutt (2022), Probabilistic Forecasting: The National Hockey League Totals Market

items.legacyLabel: CFL pregame: do we have a full efficiency literature?
items.topic: CFL pregame: do we have a full efficiency literature?
items.finding: No substantial pregame efficiency literature surfaced. The strongest peer-reviewed CFL paper uses 2015-2019 play-by-play plus pregame spread/total inputs to build calibrated in-game win probability models.
items.guidance: Use published CFL live methodology, but keep building local pregame moneyline/spread/total calibration from historical data.

provenance.legacyCitation: S. E. Hill (2022), In-game win probability models for Canadian football

items.legacyLabel: Boxing: is there any serious odds-based academic work at all?
items.topic: Boxing: is there any serious odds-based academic work at all?
items.finding: Yes, but not enough to replace local calibration. A peer-reviewed boxing demand study uses bookmaker odds, compares basic-normalization and Shin probabilities, reports an average overround near 8.9% in its sample, and explicitly treats boxing odds as information-rich but potentially strategically shaded.
items.guidance: For boxing, benchmark both basic no-vig and Shin probabilities. Treat fight-winner market separately from method/round derivatives. Still acquire historical fight odds because efficiency evidence remains sparse.

provenance.legacyCitation: Butler, Butler, Maxcy & Woodworth, Outcome Uncertainty and Viewer Demand for Basic Cable Boxing, Journal of Sports Economics

items.legacyLabel: Player props: is there strong peer-reviewed calibration research?
items.topic: Player props: is there strong peer-reviewed calibration research?
items.finding: Targeted searches still do not reveal a broad peer-reviewed player-prop efficiency literature comparable with sides/totals. Practitioner work suggests sharp-book comparison and non-uniform vig treatment matter, but this is not enough to establish production priors.
items.guidance: Props stay local-calibration-first with larger model-error margins, strict book/price verification, lineup/role/minutes inputs and stronger sample requirements.

provenance.legacyCitation: Betting Edge literature synthesis; practitioner NFL prop work retained as architecture-only evidence

items.legacyLabel: Live betting: should we assume prices incorporate new information instantly?
items.topic: Live betting: should we assume prices incorporate new information instantly?
items.finding: No. Peer-reviewed in-play soccer research finds both rapid efficiency and systematic short-lived mispricing depending on surprise. One study of 2,017 matches and ~£3B volume found expected goals were underreacted to while highly surprising goals were overreacted to, with effects fading over roughly five minutes. Other high-frequency work finds prices can update swiftly and fully around cleaner news events.
items.guidance: Live analysis requires event-surprise/state-change logic and time-since-event. Do not treat pregame fair value or immediate post-event price as automatically correct.

provenance.legacyCitation: Croxson & Reade (2014); later in-play efficiency/surprise literature

items.legacyLabel: Should live models be anchored to pregame market information?
items.topic: Should live models be anchored to pregame market information?
items.finding: Yes. Both CFL and modern in-play football modeling show that pregame market calibration is a dominant predictor of live win probability; current game state should update that strong prior rather than replace it.
items.guidance: Live Betting Edge architecture should be prior + state update: pregame market probability, then score/time/possession or sport-specific state variables.

provenance.legacyCitation: Hill 2022 CFL; Clegg et al. 2026 market-calibrated in-play football preprint

items.legacyLabel: Can sportsbook line movement itself overreact?
items.topic: Can sportsbook line movement itself overreact?
items.finding: Yes. Recent peer-reviewed work finds negative autocorrelation in moneyline changes across NFL, NBA and NHL from 2019-2023, extending earlier MLB intraday findings.
items.guidance: Track sequences of moves and reversals, not just net open-to-current movement. A move can be information, overreaction, or both at different horizons.

provenance.legacyCitation: Simon 2025

items.legacyLabel: Do statistical betting models need to maximize pick accuracy?
items.topic: Do statistical betting models need to maximize pick accuracy?
items.finding: No. A 2024 published study using NBA betting experiments finds calibration-based model selection materially outperforms accuracy-based selection for wagering decisions.
items.guidance: Use calibration/Brier/log loss/CLV/EV as core evaluation metrics. Win percentage is secondary.

provenance.legacyCitation: Walsh & Joshi (2024), Machine learning for sports betting: Should model selection be based on accuracy or calibration?

items.legacyLabel: Are player/micro props unusually sensitive to integrity risk?
items.topic: Are player/micro props unusually sensitive to integrity risk?
items.finding: Yes. Recent regulated-market actions and criminal cases show micro-props can be manipulated by a single participant without changing game outcome, leading MLB and sportsbooks to cap or restrict pitch-level wagers.
items.guidance: Micro-props get a separate integrity-risk flag, reduced confidence, smaller allowable exposure, and stronger multi-book/movement scrutiny.

provenance.legacyCitation: MLB/sportsbook integrity actions reported 2025

items.finding: Peer-reviewed CFL work exists for in-game win probability using 2015-2019 play-by-play plus pregame spread/total, but a comparable broad pregame moneyline/spread/total efficiency literature still does not surface.
items.guidance: Proceed with local CFL pregame calibration from historical odds/results. Use published CFL live models only as methodology/priors for in-game work.

items.finding: Published CFL models are well calibrated and explicitly use pregame spread/total as prior information.
items.guidance: Architect live CFL as pregame market prior + score/time/possession/state update.

evidence.legacyStatus: PARTIALLY RESOLVED — LOCAL CALIBRATION STILL REQUIRED

items.finding: Peer-reviewed boxing research uses bookmaker odds as outcome-uncertainty inputs, and modern betting-market theory strongly supports asymmetric margin/de-vig treatment. But no broad boxing efficiency literature comparable with NFL/MLB/tennis/MMA was found.
items.guidance: Build conservative fight-winner calibration from clean historical odds. Compare proportional, Shin and power-style de-vig methods. Keep book identity and overround.

items.finding: No robust peer-reviewed calibration literature surfaced for method-of-victory, round groups, exact round or total-round boxing markets.
items.guidance: Do not infer from fight-winner calibration. Add only after enough historical prices exist; use larger uncertainty and minimum-sample gates.

evidence.legacyStatus: TRUE RESEARCH GAP WITH PRACTITIONER EVIDENCE

items.finding: Broad peer-reviewed calibration research remains sparse. Practitioner NFL work over 12,624 prop bets finds book differences and favorite-longshot-shaped vig matter; a 2026 NBA thesis links FanDuel closing prop lines to player outcomes but is not a market-efficiency study.
items.guidance: Own this locally: book-aware de-vig, lineup/role/minutes/usage inputs, higher model-error margin, and strict multi-book price checks.

items.finding: Recent league/sportsbook integrity cases show participant-controlled micro outcomes can be manipulated or influenced by private information.
items.guidance: Apply explicit integrity-risk penalty and smaller maximum exposure; avoid treating apparent line moves as purely predictive.

items.finding: A 2025 peer-reviewed study of 2019-2023 moneyline movement across three sportsbooks finds significant negative autocorrelation in NFL, NBA and NHL price changes.
items.guidance: Track movement path, reversal and time since move. Never assume 'more steam = more truth'.

items.finding: Recent market-efficiency and expected-loss research shows proportional normalization can be biased when margin allocation varies with price; Shin and other transformations can be more appropriate in some markets.
items.guidance: Use proportional no-vig as baseline, but benchmark Shin/power/book-aware methods before production historical adjustments.
